clue.text: From China it developed, not new as martial art

indicators.note: developed means grown into a new form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not tells us to leave out the letter for new from the fodder

explanation.surface: Something that grew up in China, no longer novel, is presented as a fighting discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not new' removes N from CHINAIT, leaving CHIAIT, which 'developed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Tai chi is a Chinese system of slow exercise that began as a fighting style.

clue.text: A nine-month period, then another six, as primate?

indicators.note: nine months of a year is three quarters of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a year is a period of twelve months

indicators.note: six months is half a year, so only the first two letters remain

parts.note: another refers to another year

explanation.surface: A baby's nine-month gestation is followed by six more months, as an ape might expect.
explanation.walkthrough: Nine of twelve months is three of the four letters of YEAR (YEA); six months is half of YEAR (YE). The question mark flags the playful way of shortening.
explanation.definitionFit: The aye-aye is a nocturnal lemur of Madagascar, and lemurs are primates.

clue.text: Draughts in US politician's house

definitions.meaning: the board game called draughts in Britain is checkers in America, a near-identical spelling
the country residence of the British Prime Minister, in Buckinghamshire

explanation.walkthrough: Chequers is the Prime Minister's official country house; the game draughts is called checkers in the US, and chequers is also an old British name for it.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the board game also called checkers; the other is the Prime Minister's country retreat.

clue.text: What model says at work is grand

parts.note: a model would say 'I am', contracted
a model at work is posing for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: A remark by a fashion model while working is magnificent.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer split as a model's words, 'I'm posing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposing describes something impressive in size or bearing, stately and grand.

clue.text: Deliberate about maiden coming to a ball with aromatic scent

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for deliberate is wrapped round the other pieces

parts.note: to deliberate is to ponder
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone thinks hard about a young woman arriving at a dance wearing perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliberate' looks like an adjective but is the verb, giving PONDER round M and A. 'ball' is not a dance but part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pomander is a perforated sphere or mixture of spices carried for its perfume.

clue.text: Swaggering confidence in complete cure cut short with heroin injection

indicators.note: an injection puts something into the body, so the drug letter goes inside the shortened cure
cut short means its final letter is removed

parts.note: a panacea is a cure-all
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug user gets a boost of swagger from a jab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the last A off PANACEA, giving PANACE; 'injection' puts H inside, before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant style and dash, a confident swagger.

clue.text: Supporting a risky activity

parts.note: betting is gambling, a risky pastime

explanation.surface: Someone is backing a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: Abetting means aiding or encouraging, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Having no emotions in such a home

definitions.meaning: a house standing alone, not joined to any neighbour

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is aloof and uninvolved; the other is a house standing apart from its neighbours.

clue.text: Vigorous old beer — odd brew

indicators.note: a brew is something mixed and stirred together, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A strange ale has been made from a vintage recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-blooded means full of vigour and lusty energy.

clue.text: Safe to criticise children's play

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

explanation.surface: A critic is told it is risk-free to attack a show for youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER as a safe is crooks' slang, as in 'peterman', a safe-breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's stage play about the boy who never grows up is a classic family drama.

clue.text: Team of five write little

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: An instruction to write only briefly about a quintet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentad is any group or set of five, from the Greek for five.

clue.text: Giving one's notice may be very risky

definitions.meaning: giving a review, as a critic does when writing a notice of a show
a ... situation is dangerous, at a turning point

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is offering a critique of a performance; the other describes a dangerous crisis point.

clue.text: He was brought to book for his woeful predictions

definitions.text: He was brought to book for his woeful predictions

parts.words: He was brought to book for his woeful predictions
parts.note: reads as a man punished for gloomy forecasts, but means a prophet of doom who has a book of the Bible named after him

explanation.surface: A pessimistic forecaster was finally held to account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought to book' normally means punished; here it means given his own book of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament prophet lamented coming disaster, so his name now labels any doom-monger.

clue.text: Blocks broadcast with weird noises and improvised music

parts.note: to jam a broadcast is to block its signal with interference

indicators.note: weird means strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Interference on the airwaves makes strange sounds over a jazz performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam session is an informal gathering of musicians playing improvised music.

clue.text: Fool taken in by wizard's manipulation

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so the fool sits within the wizard

parts.note: a mage is a wizard or magician
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A simpleton is duped by a sorcerer's trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manipulation' suggests trickery but is the kneading of muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: Massage is the rubbing and kneading of the body by hand, a form of physical handling.

clue.text: Conrad is wrong to be cynical

indicators.note: wrong means not as it should be, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A judgement that the novelist Joseph Conrad is mistaken, delivered with a sneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonic means grimly mocking or scornful.

clue.text: After a month, article describing Pope's age

indicators.note: after places the article behind the month

parts.note: August is a month
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A month later, a newspaper piece describes the era of a pontiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope' looks like a pontiff; it is the poet Alexander Pope, of the Augustan age of English literature.
explanation.definitionFit: The Augustan age of English literature, the early eighteenth century, was the era of the poet Alexander Pope.

clue.text: Had dreadfully died after sack of ancient city

indicators.note: after places the rearranged word and the abbreviation behind the container word

parts.note: a bag is a sack

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests something mangled, so the letters of the word are scrambled

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone suffered a terrible death after the looting of an old town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' tempts as plunder but is simply a bag. 'dreadfully' rearranges HAD to HDA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iraqi capital was founded in the eighth century and was once the seat of the Abbasid caliphs.

clue.text: Nearly four feet separating horse and a woman

indicators.note: separating means coming between, so the measure sits between the horse and the letter

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse
an ell was an old cloth measure of 45 inches, just under four feet

explanation.surface: A small gap of almost a yard and a bit keeps a horse and someone apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The English ell was 45 inches, so 'nearly four feet' is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabella is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Travels with short apostolic letter over islands

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first piece above the second
short means cut down, keeping only the opening letters

parts.note: Hebrews is an epistle of the New Testament
rides means travels

explanation.surface: Someone journeys over the isles carrying a brief letter from an apostle.
explanation.walkthrough: HEB is the usual short form of Hebrews; 'short' cuts REWS from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrides are the island groups off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: After cuts in field operations, they re bound to pile up

definitions.text: After cuts in field operations, they re bound to pile up

parts.words: After cuts in field operations, they re bound to pile up
parts.note: reads like military casualties mounting, but means bundles of harvested corn tied and stacked after reaping

explanation.surface: Casualties are certain to mount after a battlefield surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' means certain on the surface and tied up in the answer; the cuts are those of a scythe in a cornfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheaves are bundles of reaped corn tied together and stacked in the field.

clue.text: Party served with prime fillet

parts.note: head as an adjective means chief or prime, as in head chef
a band is a party or group of people

explanation.surface: A banquet guest is served the best cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fillet' looks like a cut of meat; it is also an old word for a band tied round the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillet in the old sense is a ribbon or strip worn round the head to bind the hair.

clue.text: Name total idiot

parts.note: utter means total or complete

explanation.surface: Someone is labelled a complete fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutter is informal British slang for a crazy or foolish person.

clue.text: Old Jew depressed, expected to embrace another religion

parts.note: sad means depressed

indicators.note: to embrace means to hug, so the expected word holds the religious abbreviation

parts.note: due means expected, as a train is due
CE is the Church of England, a religion other than Judaism

explanation.surface: A gloomy Jewish man of old was thought likely to convert to a different faith.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sadducees were a Jewish sect of the Second Temple period, opponents of the Pharisees.

clue.text: Natural blend of tea offered by hotel

indicators.note: offered by puts the rearranged drink after the hotel that provides it

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel

indicators.note: a blend mixes things, so the letters of the drink are rearranged

explanation.surface: A guest house serves a natural mix of tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An innate quality is inborn, present by nature rather than learned.

clue.text: Give approval to girl I take out

parts.note: Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie
to date someone is to take them out

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a blessing to court a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To validate something is to confirm or ratify it officially.

clue.text: Subtlety of type of creed followed by one saint after another

parts.note: the Nicene Creed is a statement of Christian belief from the Council of Nicaea
S is the abbreviation for saint
another saint gives a second S

explanation.surface: A form of religious belief is handed down through a line of saints.
explanation.definitionFit: Niceness in its older sense means fineness of distinction, precision or delicacy.

clue.text: Engage a bishop to lead service

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the sorb is the service tree, a kind of rowan

explanation.surface: A church hires a bishop to take charge of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like worship; it is the service tree, also called the sorb.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb someone is to engage or occupy their attention completely.
